g.title: Note.3708
g.text: IUnitOfWorkTask<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken ct = default)Owned by Service: one SaveChangesAsync per use case commitsevery repository write as a single transaction.Relational aggregates only. Documents save whole (Cosmos: 1 partition, ETag).

g.title: Note.3709
g.desc: Composition root: the diamonds are DI registrations, not runt...
g.text: Composition root: the diamonds are DI registrations, not runtime ifsEach question is answered once at startup (Program.cs / host builder), never per call: Use fakes? -> register the Fake implementation instead of the real one Cache enabled? -> wrap the service/repository with the cache proxy In-process / Web services / gRPC? -> register the matching IService proxyExample for the web flow (Scrutor; the last Decorate is the outermost wrapper): services.AddScoped<IService, Service>(); if (cacheEnabled) services.Decorate<IService, ServiceCacheProxy>(); services.Decorate<IService, AuthorizationProxy>();Production code never asks about the environment; tests and local dev compose their own container.

g.title: Note.3710
g.desc: Caching: keys and invalidation ServiceCacheProxy: key = tenan...
g.text: Caching: keys and invalidationServiceCacheProxy: key = tenant + user + method + arguments, becauseAuthorizationProxy filters results per principal; never share entries across users.Service writes (CancelOrder, SubmitOrder, ...) evict the affected keys; reads use a TTL.RepositoryCacheProxy: implements the write interface (WR), so Add/Update/Deleteevict the cached entities they touch before delegating.Web flow: caching sits inside AuthorizationProxy, so nothing is served before the access check.

g.title: Note.3711
g.desc: Remote proxies map contracts <-> domain GrpcRemoteProxy: prot...
g.text: Remote proxies map contracts <-> domainGrpcRemoteProxy: proto messages <-> domain entities (generated client + mapper).WebApiRemoteProxy: JSON DTOs <-> domain entities.Controller API / Minimal API / gRPC host maps the reverse direction.Domain entities never cross the wire; contracts are versioned on their own.

g.title: Note.3725
g.desc: ETL: always through the web API The ETL tool has no local Bus...
g.text: ETL: always through the web APIThe ETL tool has no local Business Logic or Data Access Layer.It calls the web service (gRPC or Web API), so the server'sbusiness rules and AuthorizationProxy apply to every load,and nothing writes to the database directly.

g.title: Note.3726
g.desc: Offline mode (green dashed = sync) The client has its own Bus...
g.text: Offline mode (green dashed = sync)The client has its own Business Logic Layer so it can workoffline with the same rules as the web site, against Sqlite.Offline writes go to Sqlite and an outbox. On reconnectSyncService pushes the outbox through the web API, thenpulls the server changes it missed.Conflicts: the server wins (version / ETag check) and theuser is told which offline change was not applied.

g.title: Note.3727
g.desc: Repositories and storage Each aggregate has its own repositor...
g.text: Repositories and storageEach aggregate has its own repository and store (e.g. cart: Document, order: Relational).The storage model is chosen per aggregate at design time and is fixed once implemented;only the product within it can change. See Relational / Document repositories (right).

g.title: Note.3733
g.text: Relational repositoriesImplement IReadOnlyRepository / ISearchableRepository / IWriteOnlyRepository (RR / SR / WR); IUnitOfWork applies.Either implementation works with any of these databases; switching product = provider + connection string.

g.title: Note.3734
g.text: Document repositoriesImplement IReadOnlyDocumentRepository / IWriteOnlyDocumentRepository. No SR: search is not supported.No cross-document transactions (no IUnitOfWork); optimistic concurrency via ETag (_rev in CouchDB).TId carries the partition key. Switching product = rewriting the repository.

g.title: Note.3813
g.desc: Authentication (first step in every client) AuthenticationPro...
g.text: Authentication (first step in every client)AuthenticationProxy signs the user in (OIDC) and keeps the access token fresh;the remote proxies send it as a bearer token and the web API validates itbefore AuthorizationProxy runs. The desktop authenticates for everything,in-process and offline included (cached sign-in while offline).The ETL signs in as a service account (client credentials).
